current_answer: Start with the smallest sufficient layer and keep human approval separate from execution. For one welcome and occasional newsletter, an existing operated sender is first conditional option only if recipient provenance, opt-outs, review and provider outcome are recorded. In inspected Listmonk v6.2.0 tagged paths, double-opt-in confirmation changes membership and renders a page but does not send a distinct welcome. An operator-owned reviewed trigger and durable attempt ledger, or human manual action, is required for this exact job; /api/tx is a send interface, not a consent, suppression or duplicate gate. A 2 October private DOI/suppression runtime test could not run without a pinned artifact, isolated app/database, sink-only egress and teardown. Tagged source is not runtime evidence; the conditional decision and no-send boundary stand. Keila v0.30.3 remains private evaluation only with package, recovery, disclosure and sender-outcome gates open. Neither smaller tool is added to the vetted four-layer shortlist.

catalogue_card.question: Which open-source marketing projects, AI agents and harnesses are worth using, and for which tasks?
catalogue_card.text: A source-linked catalogue with conditional choices, explicit license and execution boundaries, and a draft-only first-test rule.

summary: Mautic and Activepieces CE are conditional choices for teams able to operate their platform or workflow layer.
n8n is a source-available/fair-code workflow and optional AI orchestration option; its Sustainable Use License is not OSI-style open source and may restrict commercial provision/hosting.
Marketing Agent OS is a portable harness library, not a marketing application. Its 25 September audit found a component-level provenance boundary and host-owned execution controls.
Loopmark is retained only under the direct label ‘exploratory local drafting CLI’. MarketingOS AI was examined but is not recommended or catalogued.
The research library contains dated dossiers and permanent report links for all completed research runs.
The 24 September operations guide distinguishes a local Mautic form/contact artifact from a local Activepieces CE run artifact and requires human review and teardown for either.

The 26 September Mautic 7.2.1 audit documents campaign, preference, queue, cron, role, and report surfaces while separating them from operator-owned consent, delivery, approval, monitoring, and recovery work.

The 27 September Activepieces CE audit documents the manual/local draft path, paid governance boundary, in-flight retry risk, encryption-key and multi-store recovery duties, and conflicting retention/log-cap documentation.
The 28 September synthesis assigns draft, exact-version human decision, optional CE run, sender/CRM action evidence, consent and recovery to distinct owners; no combined integration was tested.

The 29 September small-list audit keeps an existing operated sender as the first conditional option, Keila as a private-evaluation candidate only, and Listmonk as a list/campaign tool without an established built-in welcome trigger. Neither is added to the vetted four-layer shortlist.

The 30 September Keila v0.30.3 source follow-up read tagged README/build files and a registry digest listing. K1 partly advanced but remains open; K3 and X1 remain open. No image inspection, restore or send occurred, and no shortlist addition was made.

The 1 October Listmonk v6.2.0 tagged-path audit found no distinct native welcome in inspected DOI confirmation, core hook, template, campaign and transactional paths. A reviewed external trigger/ledger or manual action is required; /api/tx does not enforce consent or dedupe. No runtime test or shortlist addition.

The 2 October Listmonk v6.2.0 private DOI/suppression test did not run: pinned artifact, isolated runtime, local-only mail sink, egress proof and teardown were unavailable. A reproducible fictional-data test card was prepared; no observed behavior, send clearance or shortlist addition follows.
uncertainty: No Mautic or Activepieces CE hands-on installation, configuration, form submission, delivery, flow run, integration, or security test occurred; the controlled pilots are draft plans.
No Loopmark or MarketingOS AI hands-on install or test occurred.
Loopmark’s package/release provenance and operating/security documentation remain unresolved in the checked primary material; missing documentation is not proof a capability is absent.
License labels are component-scoped taxonomy, not legal advice or a decision on a particular deployment.
Individual connectors, permissions, costs, data paths, retry routes, and approval controls require separate verification.

Marketing Agent OS provenance was not verified file-by-file against its four upstream pins; installer collision/rollback behavior, helper effects, connector scopes, release artifacts, CI outputs, and host discovery remain unverified.

The Mautic audit was documentation and repository reading only. It did not install or operate Mautic, test delivery or suppression, or establish runtime compatibility, approval controls, secret management, connector behavior, performance, backup/restore, or production readiness.

Activepieces 0.92.0 tagged license files and exact CE UI were not verified; current unversioned Limits and Truncated Logs pages conflict, and no deployed retention, flow, retry, backup, restore, alert or deletion behavior was tested.

The 28 September cross-layer handoff is synthesis of earlier dated audits only. No new source verification, integration, external action, pilot or restore occurred. The combined route is not a recommendation.

Keila v0.30.3 exact-tag licence and extra path scope were not readable; complete tested restore, current private security disclosure route, provider-event reconciliation and real send outcomes were not established. Listmonk native form/confirmation-to-welcome trigger was not established. No installation, public form, actual contact, mail send, or restore test occurred.

The v0.30.3 tagged LICENSE.md and extra/README.md, complete archive and final image were unread. The registry digest was listed, not independently checked. No coordinated DB/upload/secret restore, rollback, private security route, plain-SMTP outcome reconciliation or exactly-once behavior was verified.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 finding is bounded to inspected tagged paths, not every customization. No install or provider receipt was obtained; read/send races, concurrent workers, ambiguous responses, provider reconciliation and exactly-once welcome outcome remain unresolved. Local git/API/raw reads partly failed and were not used as absence evidence.

The Listmonk v6.2.0 confirmation/suppression matrix, read-only candidate selector, external attempt ledger, and controlled unsubscribe/confirm race remain untested. No installed-artifact digest, private app/database, local mail sink, egress proof or teardown was available on 2 October; /api/tx was not called.
freshness_note: 2 October 2026 Listmonk private-test gate: no runtime test could run; the pinned artifact and isolated sink-only fixture were unavailable. Source-derived decision remains conditional, not send-ready.
